practice_questions.question_text: Construct recommend(items, target, score) in Python. items is nonempty; score(item, target) returns an integer suitability. Return the item with highest suitability, breaking equal-suitability ties by greater item.stock. If both are equal, keep the first item. Negative suitability is possible.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Corrects official sample lexicographic bug; retains object-list selection with primary/secondary/first-tie policy and tests counter examples.

Visits remaining items and computes suitability.
Replaces best whenever suitability is strictly higher, regardless of stock.
On equal suitability, replaces only if stock is greater.
Keeps first when both metrics tie and updates cached score with best.

practice_questions.question_text: Explain an algorithm that restores stock for a selected product using the lastn entries of a chronological singly linked sales log. Each node stores product, quantity and next; head is the old est. Add quantities only for the selected product; count n across all recent entries, leave the log unchanged, and report invalidn.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Original application rewritten to be self-contained; assessed reasoning retained within cited 2027 scope.
practice_questions.solution: Count total entries without changing links.; Reject n<0 orn greater than the log length with appropriate error handling.; Start at head and skip length-n nodes.; Traverse the remaining n recent entries.; For entries whose product is the selected product, add that quantity to its stock.; Do not alter nodes/next links or restore entries outside then-entry window.

marking_points.criterion: Count total entries without changing links.
Reject n<0 orn greater than the log length with appropriate error handling.
Start at head and skip length-n nodes.
Traverse the remaining n recent entries.
For entries whose product is the selected product, add that quantity to its stock.
Do not alter nodes/next links or restore entries outside then-entry window.
